title: Echo Audit: a methodology and toolkit for measuring whether civil society input is reflected in multilateral governance outcomes
description:
Echo Audit is a three-phase methodology and R toolkit for measuring whether civil society input into a multilateral governance process is reflected in that process's agenda and outputs, or recorded and set aside.

It extends Nelson's computational grounded theory framework (Sociological Methods & Research 49(1):3-42) with an accountability phase: the topic model discovered from civil society's own words is frozen and used as a fixed instrument to score the institution's own documents, so that all collections are measured on one comparable scale. Each theme is then classified as amplified, diluted, engulfed or excluded.

Piloted on the United Nations' first Global Dialogue on AI Governance (Geneva, 6-7 July 2026), analysing 379 civil society written submissions, 55 side-event concept notes and the 7 official session notes. The repository includes the protocol, the R implementation of all three phases, and the pilot end to end with its data and expected output.

Code is MIT licensed; the protocol and methodology documents are CC BY 4.0. The pilot corpora are public United Nations documents, redistributed for verification.
